Definition: from a compound of a derivative of G1364 and a derivative of τέμνω (to cut); to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog severely:--cut asunder (in sunder).
BiblicalUsage: To cut asunder is the judgment on the unfaithful servant, and Jesus uses it twice for the same sentence. The lord of that servant will come in a day he looks not for, and will cut him asunder and appoint his portion with the hypocrites.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the cutting asunder is a warning against presuming on delay; the servant thought his lord delayed his coming, and the delay was the very thing that exposed him.
